Admission
Graduate Admissions
Graduate Admissions
Applications for Spring 2027 will be accepted until October 1, 2026.
Applications for Fall 2027 will be accepted beginning in early September 2026, with a deadline of December 1, 2026 for full consideration.
Apply Now
Application Fee Waiver
Click to expand
All application fee waiver requests submitted by US citizens whose Bachelor's degrees were received or will be received within the last 8 years will be approved by the Self Programs Office, which awards the Self Graduate Fellowship to a few select incoming domestic students in STEM disciplines each year. If you are interested in having your application fee waived, please complete the Application Fee Waiver Request Form located on the Graduate Admissions website. Before submitting a fee waiver request, you must first start a graduate admission application and select the program you're applying to - fee waiver requests without a program will be denied. Your application fee is non-refundable, so do not pay the application fee when you submit your admission application if you plan to submit a fee waiver request.
More information on the fee waiver can be found on the Graduate Admissions website.
Application Deadlines
Click to expand
Spring 2027: The deadline for priority consideration is October 1, 2026.
Fall 2027: The deadline for priority consideration is December 1, 2026.
Applications past the Fall 2027 priority deadline will still be considered, but we will begin reviewing applications starting on December 1, so you are encouraged to submit your application prior to that date to ensure that you are given first consideration.
Please submit your application through the Apply website.
You will need the following for your application:
Transcripts: A scanned version of the transcript from your undergraduate and any post-Bachelor institution(s). (If admitted, you will be required to submit official transcripts from all post-secondary schools attended.)
Recommendations: You will be asked for the names and email addresses of three people who can write a recommendation letter describing your qualifications for graduate school in chemistry. Once you submit the application, an email will be sent requesting a letter from each person that you name.
Resume/CV and Personal Statement
International Students: Proof of English proficiency, as required by the Office of Graduate Studies. To be considered for GTA/GRA support, you must be admitted on regular status. GTA positions have additional requirements that includes at least a 22 on the Speaking section of the TOEFL test (or 7 in Speaking on IELTS).
The Department of Chemistry will review your application only after the application process is complete. Please contact the Graduate Program Coordinator, Ross Perryman (rossp@ku.edu), with any questions about the application process.
